cards.text: Soon afterward, Jesus heads to a town called Nain. And friend, He is NOT walking there by Himself.

cards.question: Who's walking with Jesus on the way to the town of Nain?

answers.text: His disciples and a large crowd

cards.text: As Jesus gets close to the town gate, something is coming out the other way. It's a dead man, being carried out of town.

cards.question: The dead man being carried out of Nain is the ___ son of his mother.
The dead man's mother still has her husband to lean on.

cards.text: She's a widow who just lost her only son, and a large crowd from the town is walking with her. Jesus's crowd going in, her crowd coming out, one gate: that's a stadium with ONE exit open.

cards.question: When the Lord sees the grieving widow at the gate, what does He have for her?
Then Jesus speaks to the widow. What does He tell her?

cards.text: Then Jesus goes right up to the funeral procession and touches the coffin. In front of BOTH crowds.

cards.question: What do the men carrying the coffin do when Jesus touches it?

cards.text: Everybody frozen in place. I KNOW that freeze, friend. That was the whole junk drawer every single time the light came in.

cards.question: With His hand on the coffin, Jesus speaks again. Who is He talking to this time?

answers.text: The young man in the coffin

cards.text: "Young man," He said, "I tell you, get up!" That's it. No speech, no ceremony. Just get up.

cards.question: After Jesus speaks, the dead man sits up and begins to speak.

cards.text: SAT UP. TALKING. I spent years in a junk drawer thinking that was the end of my story, and this man was already on his way out of town!

cards.question: Then Jesus gives the young man back to his ___.
A sense of awe sweeps over everyone there, and they glorify God.
The people say a great ___ has appeared among them.

cards.text: And they say, "God has visited His people!" Two crowds came to that gate going opposite directions, and now they're ALL saying the same thing.

cards.question: The news about what Jesus did stays inside the town of Nain.

findings.problem: The stadium comparison doesn't share the core action. The scene is two crowds moving in opposite directions through one gate. A stadium with one exit open is everyone leaving the same way. The image doesn't click without explaining.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The card that reveals a widow has just lost her only son turns the funeral procession into a crowd-traffic gag in the same breath. That doesn't fit the moment or treat her situation with respect.

rule.text: Humor about people in Bible stories looks at their human situation with respect.

findings.problem: The right answer "Do not weep" sounds like Bible wording. "Go on home" and "Wait for Me here" sound casual and modern, so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: "Everybody frozen in place" stretches the text. Luke 7:14 says only that those carrying the coffin stood still.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: This card tells no new part of the passage. It only reacts to the answer on card 10 with a joke.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: This card restates the answer to card 14 (he sat up and spoke) and adds nothing new from the passage, so it works as a recap card.
The punchline "this man was already on his way out of town" doesn't land. It's unclear how being carried out dead relates to Papa Dorin thinking his story was over. A stranger would say "huh?"

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: Few lines across the walkthrough get a real laugh. Cards 1, 13 and 19 read as pleasant narration, and the main jokes (cards 6, 11, 15) have the issues above. The walkthrough doesn't reach laugh-out-loud funny.

rule.text: But he is FUNNY. Not mildly amusing. Laugh-out-loud funny, the kind a baker repeats to a friend.
